title: Flight Mechanics
full_title: Flight Mechanics: Performance, Stability and Control
tagline: Aircraft performance, range and endurance, manoeuvres, take-off and landing, static stability and trim, equations of motion, dynamic modes and flight control
summary: Flight mechanics predicts how an aircraft flies: how fast, how far and how high it can go, whether it is stable, and how it is controlled. The course covers steady-flight performance, range and endurance, turns and take-off and landing, longitudinal and lateral–directional static stability and trim, the rigid-body equations of motion, the dynamic modes of an aircraft, and an introduction to stability augmentation and autopilots.

chapters.title: Steady flight performance
chapters.summary: The standard atmosphere and airspeeds, drag polars, thrust and power required and available, maximum speed, climb and gliding flight.

chapters.title: Range and endurance
chapters.summary: The Breguet equations for jet and propeller aircraft, and the best speeds for range and endurance.

chapters.title: Manoeuvres, take-off and landing
chapters.summary: Turning flight, load factor and the V–n diagram, and take-off and landing distances.

chapters.title: Longitudinal static stability and trim
chapters.summary: Pitching moment, the neutral point and static margin, trim with the elevator, and stick-fixed and stick-free stability.

chapters.title: Lateral–directional static stability
chapters.summary: Directional and roll stability, the dihedral effect, and rudder and aileron control.

chapters.title: Aircraft equations of motion
chapters.summary: Body axes and Euler angles, the rigid-body equations of motion, stability derivatives and linearisation about trim.

chapters.title: Dynamic stability and aircraft modes
chapters.summary: The phugoid and short-period modes, Dutch roll, roll subsidence and the spiral mode, and handling qualities.

chapters.title: Introduction to flight control
chapters.summary: Stability augmentation, autopilots and fly-by-wire control laws.
